hook.text: Sildenafil and tadalafil don't create blood flow on their own. They stop your body from switching one signal off.

vessel.text: Healthy erectile function depends on blood flow. Zoom into one of the small arteries that supply the tissue. It's wrapped in smooth muscle, which at rest stays tense, so the artery stays narrow.

signal.text: When the body sends the right signal, nerves and the vessel lining release nitric oxide. It enters the muscle cell and switches on an enzyme that makes a messenger molecule, cyclic G M P.

relax.text: Cyclic G M P tells the muscle to relax. Calcium leaves the cell, the artery widens, and more blood flows in.

pde5.text: But the body builds in an off switch. An enzyme called P D E 5 breaks cyclic G M P down, and the signal fades.

inhibit.text: Sildenafil and tadalafil are P D E 5 inhibitors. These blue molecules fit into the enzyme's active site and block it, so cyclic G M P lasts longer, and the artery stays relaxed.

timing.text: They only work with the body's own signal, because without nitric oxide there's nothing to protect. The main difference is time. Sildenafil's half-life is about four hours. Tadalafil's is about seventeen.

safety.text: These drugs also relax other vessels, which is why mixing them with nitrate medicines can drop blood pressure dangerously. Same enzyme, same vessels, different timing.
